bandReport.notes:
COMPLETE — Q1-Q26 across p00-p03, contiguous with no gaps. Band opens the paper, so Q1 is the paper's first question and there is no preceding page to check.

SEAMS: p03 ends with Q26 whole (stem + all four options). p04 was opened but NOT transcribed; it opens cleanly with a fresh Q27, so the p03/p04 seam strands nothing and truncates nothing. Within the band, three questions straddle a COLUMN break on their own page and were read across it: Q10 (stem + statements I/II bottom-left of p01, 'Select the answer using the code given below :' + options top-right of the same page), Q13 (stem bottom-right of p01, options continue on the same column), Q23 (stem bottom-left of p03, options top-right of p03).

FIGURES: NONE. Every page of this band was examined at full resolution and there is no printed diagram, graph, chart or geometric figure anywhere in Q1-Q26. Q19 (triangle ABC with an altitude AD) and Q18 (angles of depression from a bridge) are the two items that could plausibly have carried one; both are stated entirely in words and print no figure. No question in the band sets hasFigure.

DIRECTIONS / SETS: NONE. No 'Directions:' block and no 'Consider the following for the next N items' block appears anywhere in p00-p03, so this band opens no set and inherits none. Q10, Q13 and Q28 (p04, not mine) use the 'Consider the following statements I / II' form, but that is a self-contained single question whose statements live in its own stem — not a shared stimulus over several numbered items. No question in the band carries context or setLabel.

DATA TABLES: NONE.

MISPRINT FLAGGED: Q18 option (b) is printed with a capital H ('H tan(alpha).tan(beta)') where the stem defines the height as lower-case h, and options (a), (c), (d) all use lower-case h. Verified at 8x zoom off the source PDF. Transcribed as printed, not repaired.

INVENTED SUBTOPIC: Q2 — 'Difference of Squares and Factor Pairs' under Number System. The technique is factor-pairing 72 as (m-n)(m+n) with a same-parity constraint; no listed Number System subtopic covers difference-of-squares counting, and forcing it into 'Perfect Squares and Cubes' or 'Factors, Multiples, HCF and LCM' would misdescribe it.

AMBIGUOUS GLYPHS RESOLVED AT ZOOM (6-8x, off the source PDF): Q4 exponents 222/333/444; Q5 the two long factors 4321012345 and 98766789; Q8 the surd chain endpoints (sqrt(10)+sqrt(9)) ... (sqrt(196)+sqrt(195)); Q10 statements I and II; Q11 8 sin(theta) - 4 sin^2(theta); Q12 the option set; Q14 the inequality chain and both tan values; Q16 the exponents sin^2/cos^2 and the RHS 16; Q17 all four options (the 1/2 factor distinguishes (a) from (b) and (c) from (d)); Q18 the capital-H misprint; Q19 the given sides; Q20 the equation; Q25 the exponent 255; Q26 the exponents 97 and 54. Nothing in the band was left unreadable.

NOTATION: printed decimals use a raised middle dot (Q1 options, Q23 options) and are written with a full stop per the brief. Q23 prints the rupee glyph and is written 'Rs.' per the brief. Both flagged on their rows.

questions.stem: A real number \(x\) is such that the sum of the number and four times its square is the least. What is that number ?
questions.subtopic: Maximum and Minimum of Quadratic Expressions

questions.stem: The difference of the square of two natural numbers \(m\) and \(n\) \((m > n)\) is 72. How many pairs of natural numbers will satisfy ?
questions.subtopic: Difference of Squares and Factor Pairs
flags: Invented subtopic — the technique is factor-pairing of 72 under (m-n)(m+n) with a parity constraint; no listed Number System subtopic covers difference-of-squares counting.

questions.stem: Let \(N\) be a 5-digit number. When \(N\) is divided by 6, 12, 15, 24 it leaves respectively 2, 8, 11, 20 as remainders. What is the greatest value of \(N\) ?

What is the remainder when
\(111^{222} + 222^{333} + 333^{444}\)
is divided by 5 ?

What are the last three digits in the multiplication of
\(4321012345 \times 98766789\) ?
\(p\) varies directly as \((x^2 + y^2 + z^2)\). When \(x = 1\), \(y = 2\), \(z = 3\), then \(p = 70\). What is the value of \(p\) when \(x = -1\), \(y = 1\), \(z = 5\) ?
Let \(N\) be the least positive multiple of 11 that leaves a remainder of 5 when divided by 6, 12, 15, 18. Which one of the following is correct ?
What is \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{10} + \sqrt{9}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{11} + \sqrt{10}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{12} + \sqrt{11}} + \ldots + \frac{1}{\sqrt{196} + \sqrt{195}}\) equal to ?

Train \(X\) crosses a man standing on the platform in 24 seconds and train \(Y\) crosses a man standing on the platform in 18 seconds. They cross each other while running in opposite directions in 20 seconds. What is the ratio of speed of \(X\) to speed of \(Y\) ?

Let \(p, q\) be the roots of the equation \(x^2 + mx - n = 0\) and \(m, n\) be the roots of the equation \(x^2 + px - q = 0\) \((m, n, p, q\) are non-zero numbers). Which of the following statements is/are correct ?

I. \(m(m + n) = -1\)

II. \(p + q = 1\)

Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.subtopic: Vieta's Relations and Root Coefficient Identities

questions.stem: What is the maximum value of \(8\sin\theta - 4\sin^2\theta\) ?
questions.subtopic: Maximum and Minimum of Trigonometric Expressions

questions.stem: What is \((1 + \tan\alpha\,\tan\beta)^2 + (\tan\alpha - \tan\beta)^2\) equal to ?

Consider the following statements :

I. \(\tan 50^\circ - \cot 50^\circ\) is positive

II. \(\cot 25^\circ - \tan 25^\circ\) is negative

Which of the statements is/are correct ?

If \(0 \le (\alpha - \beta) \le (\alpha + \beta) \le \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \sqrt{3}\) and \(\tan(\alpha - \beta) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), then what is \(\tan\alpha \cdot \cot 2\beta\) equal to ?
What is the value of \(\sin^2\theta \cos^2\theta (\sec^2\theta + \mathrm{cosec}^2\theta)\) equal to ?
If \(64^{\sin^2\theta} + 64^{\cos^2\theta} = 16\) where \(0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}\), then what is the value of \(\tan\theta + \cot\theta\) ?
If \(\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta - \cot\theta = m\) and \(\sec\theta - \tan\theta = n\), then what is \(\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta + \sec\theta\) equal to ?

From a point \(X\) on a bridge across a river, the angles of depression of two points \(P\) and \(Q\) on the banks on opposite side of the river are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) respectively. If the point \(X\) is at a height \(h\) above the surface of the river, what is the width of the river if \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are complementary ?
flags: Printed misprint preserved: option (b) is set with a capital \(H\) while the stem defines the height as lower-case \(h\); every other option uses \(h\). Verified at 8x zoom.
